title: AI Learning Roadmap by Role
description: Build a realistic 90-day AI roadmap tailored to your role: student, manager, marketer, analyst, founder, or developer.

data.text: AI mastery is role-dependent. A marketer, analyst, and software engineer should not follow the same plan. The fastest path is to prioritize workflows you run every week, then build depth where the return is highest.

If you are a student or early-career professional, optimize for portfolio proof, communication clarity, and repeatable research habits. Your roadmap should focus on outputs you can show: better notes, stronger analyses, clearer writing, and structured project artifacts that demonstrate consistent improvement over 12 weeks.

rows: Portfolio case studies + interview story rehearsal

data.text: Most people stall because they pick interesting workflows, not high-leverage ones. In the first 30 days, choose two workflows that happen frequently, consume noticeable time, and have clear quality criteria. This creates quick confidence and measurable gains before you expand your stack.

data.title: Create your personal 12-week AI plan
data.description: Design a practical roadmap grounded in your actual weekly work.
steps: List your top 5 repetitive tasks by time spent.
Map each task to one AI use case and one tool.
Prioritize by impact x ease and pick top 2 for month one.
Define quality checks so output remains trustworthy.
Schedule a weekly 30-minute review to refine your stack.
data.expectedOutcome: You leave with a realistic, role-specific AI execution roadmap.

data.title: Roadmap principles
points: Role context determines the right AI stack
Start with weekly tasks, not shiny new tools
Measure value in hours saved and quality improved
Add complexity only after baseline workflows are stable
Review and adapt monthly as tools evolve

data.title: Common roadmap mistakes to avoid
points: Trying five tools at once before one workflow is stable
Tracking activity instead of measurable outcomes
Skipping quality checks because outputs look polished
Copying someone else's stack without role fit
Failing to revisit prompts and templates after each month

data.title: Role comparison: time to first value

cards.title: Manager
cards.description: First value in 1-2 weeks: meeting summaries and decision memos. Low technical barrier, high visibility.

cards.title: Marketer
cards.description: First value in 2-3 weeks: idea generation and content briefs. Requires tone and brand context setup.

cards.title: Analyst
cards.description: First value in 3-4 weeks: data cleanup and KPI summaries. Needs clean data sources and formatting rules.

cards.title: Developer
cards.description: First value in 1-2 weeks: code explanation and test generation. Leverages existing technical knowledge.

data.title: Realistic 90-day roadmap example
data.content:
Role: Marketing Manager at B2B SaaS

Days 1-30:
- Week 1: Set up Claude Pro with custom instruction: 'I write for CTOs and IT directors. Professional but approachable tone.'
- Week 2: Draft 3 blog post ideas and 1 LinkedIn carousel using AI
- Week 3: Create a prompt template for weekly campaign briefs
- Week 4: Measure time saved vs. manual drafting

Days 31-60:
- Build channel-specific prompt templates (email, LinkedIn, blog)
- Add a quality checklist: brand voice check, fact check, CTA clarity
- Use AI to analyze last quarter's top-performing content and identify patterns

Days 61-90:
- Automate weekly performance summaries
- Build a prompt library for the whole marketing team
- Measure ROI: hours saved, content velocity, engagement lift

data.title: Pro tip
data.text: The fastest way to build your AI stack is to document one workflow per week in a shared prompt library. After 12 weeks, you have 12 reusable workflows — a complete personal AI system.
